title: Forward 32-byte record copy construction
summary: Recovered VA 0x520c40, size 76 from accepted assembly and direct Game.exe disassembly. Copies a 16-byte snapshot followed by four sequential 4-byte snapshots per record, skips stores for a zero destination cursor, advances both cursors 32 bytes, and returns the destination cursor. Callers use ECX begin, EDX end, stack destination and caller cleanup; portable implementation exposes an ordinary C++ function. Fields remain opaque.
test_description: Direct original comparison using a GCC regparm(3) adapter for the custom register ABI. Tests zero through six records, unaligned disjoint buffers, self copies, forward/backward overlaps at offsets 1..36, five byte patterns, empty null range and null destination for a singleton. Checks returned pointers and every buffer byte, including untouched regions. Local GCC i386 oracle execution returned zero; oracle section compared equal to all 76 original bytes. Implementation compiled with pinned MSVC2013 under O1, O2 and O2 /Oy-.
known_limits: Record field types and owning container identity are unresolved; callers indicate allocation/insertion range copies.
Invalid or unreachable end pointers, inaccessible memory and null destination with multiple records can fault or fail to terminate in the original and are not executed.

Portable function does not reproduce the original custom register ABI. Integer cursors model the original 32-bit address arithmetic on the target platform; 64-bit native ports use native pointer width.
No byte matching claim; overlap behavior checked on bounded accessible buffers. No exceptions or OS dependencies occur in this routine.
